ops.title: Product workers reach multi-GiB RSS and read tens of GiB from disk on monorepo drive roots
ops.premise:
Premise: the product-worker growth seen on 2026-10-12 (worker 22437, root monorepo/sole shard 7, 8.4 to 12.7 GiB RSS in a minute at 157% CPU on 12.93.2) comes from Python-level file reading inside the worker during a hook dispatch, not from transcript warming and not from the snapshot owner.

Evidence at 00:07-00:10 PDT 2026-10-13 on 12.93.2:
- Worker 78633 replaced 22437 on the same root and shard. RSS 7.49 GiB, physical footprint 0.23 GiB, 34.45 GiB physical disk reads in 14 minutes (proc_pid_rusage).
- A 3 s stack sample of 78633 at 96% CPU reports peak footprint 7.4 GiB. On-CPU frames are read(2), Python text decoding, and the json scanner (scanstring_unicode, scan_once_unicode), plus open and stat. No sqlite frames.
- Five workers hold 56.4 of the 58.5 GiB the 43 workers read. All five serve monorepo drive roots (sole, limpet, sturgeon, alewife) on shards 5 and 7. The other 37 have a median of 0.05 GiB.
- The snapshot owner read 17.5 GiB in the same 29 minutes.
- The sole shard-7 log shows a Stop dispatch of 25005 ms with note_flushed_lanes, escalate_unrotated_lanes and ask_lanes_to_rotate abandoned.

Not established: which file is read and which hook reads it.
Artifacts: /tmp/ram-pressure-refresh-20261012-2335/warm-delivery-before-sample-78633.txt, warm-delivery-before-1.json, warm-delivery-before-lsof-78633.txt.

ops.text: PR #360 removes the per-worker warm scheduler and does not touch in-worker file reads; measure per-worker disk reads and peak footprint on 12.93.3 to confirm the growth is independent of warming.
